video_title: Windy says Wemby was 'visualizing' being in the NBA Finals at 13 years old 😯 | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama visualized his current success since he was thirteen
quotes.excerpt: He was visualizing this when he was 13. He's like, this is what I want to be.
quotes.quote: He's embraced that. Seriously, when he was 13, he talked about visualization two games in advance. That's not true. He was visualizing this when he was 13. He's like, this is what I want to be. And he said something, my favorite thing he said there was that impatience can be a virtue. What he's saying is, don't talk to me about what I'm supposed to wait for. I want it today. And that's the way he's approached his entire career. That's the way he's going to approach this series.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama shows maturity and leadership beyond his years
quotes.excerpt: He's very mature and the fact that it's going to take step, they're going through it right now.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: I like to consider myself a mature young person at 22, but he's unbelievably mature.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: I'm glad you did because he did. I was not doing that. He's very mature and the fact that it's going to take step, they're going through it right now. Impatience can be a virtue. He's not trying to wait. He doesn't care about any of those things.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins relates to Victor Wembanyama's desire for greatness
quotes.excerpt: I envy and I'm jealous of people that's greater than me because I want their greatness.
quotes.quote: Wemby and I relate. We relate because mentality-wise, I'm a guy that I envy and I'm jealous of people that's greater than me because I want their greatness. Wemby wants greatness. So when he sees someone that's ahead of him that has accomplished more than him, he envies them. And that's okay in the game of basketball. For example, James Posey was on our team in 2008. He was the only champion outside of Sam Cassell. But every game day on the road, he used to wear his suit and that damn championship ring with Miami. And he used to make sure he wore it on the outside hand so when you walk by you could see it. And it used to piss everybody off. And I went up to him one day, Posey, and I was like, damn, bro, like why you got to throw it in our face? He was like, well, go win one. And I said, you know, right? That's real. And I get that from Wemby. Like he don't care, he's chasing greatness.

quotes.speaker: Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns reflects on his first NBA Finals appearance
quotes.excerpt: For my career, I've only been able to see that Finals logo on TV.
quotes.quote: It means a lot, you know, because for my career, I've only been able to see that Finals logo on TV. So it means a lot to be the person that sees the logo on their jersey and has this opportunity. So the word grateful is all I could say.

quotes.speaker: Josh Hart
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Hart questions his own performance during the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I'm like, damn, you know, am I ass? Like do I suck as a basketball player?
quotes.quote: There were moments I went home and I'm like, I'm like, damn, you know, am I ass? Like do I suck as a basketball player? There was a lot of those moments. Whenever your minutes go down or you get benched, you have that thought process. Now I'm cool with it sometimes. I mean, there was what, Game 1 I got benched, and Land was out there hooping and I was happy about it.

quotes.speaker: Malika Andrews
quotes.summary_phrase: Defending Karl-Anthony Towns is the biggest strategic question
quotes.excerpt: Who defends Karl-Anthony Towns and what does the trickle-down effect end up being?

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: I think the single biggest question here is who defends Karl-Anthony Towns and what does the trickle-down effect end up being?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: So remember there's two different types of Karl-Anthony Towns. You have Karl-Anthony Towns the big man, you have Karl-Anthony Towns the point center. I would expect Devin Vassell to be an early option. They could also use Steph Curry, but Curry I think is going to be on to Jalen Brunson. So what you're looking for there is you can still, you want Wemby to be the support defender. I like how our colleague Aman Shampert calls what Karl-Anthony Towns does the cat scan where he gets the ball, holds it way up in the air and looks for a place to go. Well, you can take away those passing angles if you were to put 7'5" guy on him. So that's an antidote that they can go to for sure.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Spurs will use a mix of defensive strategies against Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: You can't give any superstar a steady diet of one thing. They're going to double him some.
quotes.quote: I'd assume they do a mix of both. You can't give any superstar a steady diet of one thing. They're going to double him some, they're going to be in gaps some, especially with the weapons he has around him with OG and way Mikal Bridges is knocking down shots and then Landry Shamet of course off the bench. So they can't just double him all game. But I imagine they will mix up Wemby on cat as well. They'll have Vassell on him some, they might have Steph Curry on him some, they might have Fox, they'll switch. Especially when he's on the perimeter. He's on the perimeter, he'll be able to pass, but those guards can get up into him so he won't be able to shoot the three as much. But if he goes down to that post, which is going to be a mismatch for those guards because cat has a different mentality than Chet, they're going to have to put Wemby on him. He's going to have to switch. He's going to have to stay at the rim but when the big comes down whether it's Mitchell Robinson or Karl-Anthony Towns, I'd imagine Mitchell Johnson will have Wemby switch onto the big so there's not much of a mismatch where he can score and pass out of the double team, which gives the Knicks such an advantage on offense that they'll run the score up.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: The battle of the benches will determine the series outcome
quotes.excerpt: I think the X-factor that's going to determine this series are the battle of the benches.
quotes.quote: I think the X-factor that's going to determine this series or the battle of the benches, right? Like between Spurs and OKC. When you look at Spurs, you talking about Dylan Harper who had some fantastic moments throughout this postseason. Kelden Johnson, and then when you look at the Knicks, you talking about Landry Shamet, Mitchell Robinson, McBride, all of those guys. And look, right there, this is the bench scoring this postseason between the two and it's pretty much even. So it's it's it's something because, you know, like we at the rodeo, right? We at the rodeo and I'm looking at those two bulls in particular, Landry Shamet and Dylan Harper, who's going to win that battle?
